detailed_rationale:
Home First Finance is an affordable-housing-finance company (HFC) targeting first-time homebuyers earning below Rs.50,000/month, with an average ticket size of ~Rs.12 lakh and housing loans representing 83% of AUM. This is a structurally attractive, underpenetrated segment of Indian retail credit, and the company's execution has been consistently strong: AUM reached Rs.16,938 Cr in Q1 FY27, up 25.7% YoY, with record quarterly disbursements of Rs.1,628 Cr and PAT up 34.5% YoY to Rs.160 Cr. Management has explicitly guided to sustain ~25% AUM growth through FY27, and the company has a track record of hitting similar guidance in recent periods. Management commentary describes asset quality as stable, though specific GNPA/NNPA figures were not available in the sources we reviewed, so we treat 'stable' as a qualitative management claim rather than a verified hard number.

On ownership: promoter holding is only 6.98% (down from 33.7% in 2021), but this reflects the company's original private-equity sponsors (True North and Bessemer Venture Partners, both classified as 'promoter' pre-IPO) progressively selling down post-listing, a standard PE-exit pattern rather than a distress signal -- and institutional replacement has been strong (FIIs 43.9%, DIIs 29.8%), arguably a vote of confidence rather than a concern. D/E of ~2.43 is normal and expected for an HFC business model (financial-sector leverage exemption applies) and is not a red flag on its own.

Our own quant data shows several key fields blank for this name -- ROCE, interest coverage, and 3-year revenue CAGR are all missing from the scored universe -- which likely means the Sell classification here is at least partly a function of incomplete inputs rather than a full, fairly-computed score. Reverse-DCF: at ~23.5x earnings for a business growing AUM at 25%+ with a demonstrated execution track record and financial-sector-normal leverage, the valuation looks reasonable rather than rich, particularly against ROE of 13.6%, which is respectable though not exceptional for the sector.
recommendation_rationale: We are rescuing the quant Sell to Hold. The observable fundamentals -- 25.7% AUM growth, 34.5% PAT growth, management guidance for continued ~25% growth, management-reported stable asset quality, and a reasonable ~23.5x valuation for that growth profile -- do not support a Sell call, and our own quant data shows material coverage gaps (ROCE, interest coverage, and 3-year revenue CAGR all blank) that likely handicapped the scoring for this name. The elevated D/E is business-model-normal for an HFC and exempted under our standard financial-sector treatment, and the low promoter percentage reflects known PE-sponsor exits rather than distress.
summary: Home First Finance is a technology-driven affordable-housing lender targeting first-time homebuyers. AUM grew 25.7% year-on-year to Rs.16,938 Cr in the most recent quarter with profit up 34.5%, and management has guided to sustain roughly 25% AUM growth. At about 23.5 times earnings, this looks like a reasonable price for that growth rate, and our own quantitative dataset appears to have gaps (several coverage-ratio fields were missing) that we believe explain the Sell classification more than any genuine fundamental weakness. We rate this a Hold.
positive_para: Genuinely strong, consistent execution -- AUM up 25.7% YoY to Rs.16,938 Cr, record disbursements, PAT up 34.5% -- in a structurally underpenetrated segment (affordable housing finance) with management guiding to sustain similar growth into FY27, backed by a technology-driven underwriting model and strong institutional ownership (FIIs 43.9%, DIIs 29.8%).
negative_para: We could not verify hard GNPA/NNPA asset-quality figures independently -- 'stable' asset quality is a management characterization we have not cross-checked against a disclosed number, and affordable housing finance is a competitive segment facing incursion from banks and other HFCs that could pressure yields or growth if the current pace cannot be sustained. Our own quant coverage for this name is incomplete (ROCE, interest coverage, 3-year revenue CAGR all missing), which limits how confidently we can benchmark it against better-covered peers.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~23.5x earnings against 25%+ guided AUM growth and an ROE of 13.6%, the valuation is reasonable, not rich -- it does not require heroic assumptions beyond what management itself is guiding, and elevated D/E is normal for the HFC business model rather than a leverage red flag.
